    Features

    Every Archie feature, by area

    287 features in 18 areas. Each one opens to where it is in Archie, how to use it, and its limits.

    287 features

    Talking to your agent

    • Stop a reply partway

      Type stop, or press Stop under the reply, while your agent is working; what it already finished stays done and nothing more happens.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.5
    • Tables and checklists in replies

      In Archie, your agent can answer with a table or a checklist when that is the clearer shape, and links and code show properly.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.1
    • New chat

      Press New chat and your agent starts fresh. It forgets the conversation and keeps what it has learned about you.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Question cards keep their buttons

      The cards where your agent offers choices keep working for two weeks, even after Archie restarts, so a card from Friday still answers on Monday.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • What your agent saved and looked at

      Under a reply, Archie says what your agent saved to your lists, with Open and Undo, and what it read to answer.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Ask your agent ordinary questions

      Your agent answers ordinary questions the way any AI chat does, such as how to word a hard email, in the same conversation as everything else it does.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.3
    • Your agent looks back through your conversation

      Your agent keeps the last twenty messages in front of it. Ask about something from further back and it searches your conversation for it.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.1
    • Search this chat

      Type a word or a name and Archie shows every message in your chat with an agent that has all of them, newest first. Press one to go to it.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Charts in the conversation

      Ask for a chart and your agent draws it in the conversation as bars, a line or a pie, with the numbers on it.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • The Today line over the message box

      One line over the message box says what changed and what went out today, like "Today: 4 changes, 1 sent". Press it for the list, each change with Open and Undo.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Not now, answered at once

      Press Not now, No thanks, Skip or Cancel under something your agent offered, and Archie answers "Okay, left it." right away, without asking the AI, and drops what the card offered.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Yes, answered at once

      Press Confirm or just say yes under a change your agent is waiting on, and Archie makes the change right away, without asking the AI, and tells you it's done.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.18
    • Your presses, shown as presses

      A button you press shows on your side of the chat as that button, pressed, over the first words of the card it answered. Confirm says the change it confirms, and a press never changes your agent's words.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Replies in your lists' own words

      Your agent names a change by the column's name on your list, like For. It says what it did, like "I looked it up online", and leaves out Archie's own words, such as skill and specialist. Who's Got This keeps its list as Who has what.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Unasked messages wait for the answer

      Messages your agent sends without being asked, like the morning list, a card about new mail or a routine's report, wait until it has finished answering you.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Unasked messages say so

      When your agent sends something without being asked, a line over it says so and what it is, like "Sent on its own at 6:30 AM: your morning list."

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Links Archie never read are cut back

      If a reply holds a web link to a site Archie never read or found in a search, the link is cut back to the site's front page.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11
    • /pending moves waiting cards down

      Type /pending and everything still waiting on you is posted again at the bottom of the chat. The earlier copy says the newest card replaced it, and its buttons go.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Rooms: several of your agents in one conversation

      Put two or more of your agents in one conversation, called a room. The one you name answers and the others stay quiet, and a message that names nobody goes to whichever agent answered last.

      • On your computer
      • Not in Archie for Teams
      • Since 0.2.5
    • Answers appear as they are written

      In the Archie window, on an Anthropic key of your own and on an agent with no chat app connected, your agent's answer starts to show while the AI is still writing it, instead of after it is finished.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.0
    • Suggested asks in an empty chat

      An empty chat suggests up to three things you can ask your agent right now, picked from the skills it has and the accounts you connected. Tap one and it goes as if you had typed it.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.12
    • Commands typed in the chat

      Typing / in the message box lists the commands: /new, /voice, /text, /stop, /pending, /quiet, /skills, /invite, /help and /start.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.3
    • A long job checks in, and stops at eight minutes

      A job that takes a while says what it is doing at 45 seconds, 2, 4 and 6 minutes, with how to call it off, and stops on its own at eight minutes, or fifteen when your agent may use websites or Mac apps.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.2.5
    • Ask what your agent got done

      Ask what your agent got done and it answers from its own record of jobs, saying what each job changed and whether each email it drafted went out.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.2.0
    • Copy chat

      One press copies the whole conversation as text, and select all selects only the chat.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.1
    • A reply shows the message it answers

      A message you send as a reply shows the start of the message it answers, and the chat follows the newest message until you scroll away.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.10

    Voice

    • Say a message instead of typing

      Press the microphone beside the message box to speak a message; Archie turns it into words on your computer, and only the words go to your AI company.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.3
    • Voice notes on chat apps, and spoken replies in a voice you pick

      A voice note sent on Telegram, Discord, Slack, Matrix, iMessage, Archie Mobile or in Archie's window is turned into words on this computer, and your agent can answer out loud in one of 28 voices you pick, when you spoke to it, every time, or never. Slack and Signal get written answers.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.3
    • A voice note's written answer is made to be read out

      Send your agent a voice note on a chat app, and the answer it writes back is made for your phone to read aloud: a table comes as one sentence a row, and a link's address goes after the answer.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.13
    • Spoken replies on iMessage come as audio messages

      On iMessage, when your agent answers out loud, the answer comes as an audio message in the Messages thread, instead of a file to open somewhere else.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.12

    Your phone

    • Archie Mobile

      Archie Mobile, for iPhone and Android, reaches the agent on your computer, which locks every message with a key that only your phone also holds.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.1
    • Pick where your agent answers, and disconnect a chat app

      On an agent's Setup tab, picking Archie Mobile or a connected chat app is what moves your agent there, and Disconnect takes a chat app off that one agent.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.14
    • One computer at a time has your phone

      With Archie on two computers signed in to the same account, Archie Mobile reads the one whose code it scanned last, and the other one says so.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.15
    • Your agent on iMessage, with its own Apple ID

      On a Mac, your agent answers in iMessage in the chat you have with yourself, with its name on its replies, or on an Apple ID of its own.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.6
    • Notifications on Archie Mobile

      Turn on notifications in Archie Mobile and your phone shows reminders, reports, new mail, and replies to what you sent from it, even with the app closed.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.9
    • A phone message waits for a sleeping computer

      A message sent from Archie Mobile while your computer sleeps waits and says so, and your agent answers it when the computer wakes, knowing it was sent earlier.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.5
    • Run a routine or tune a skill from your phone

      From Archie Mobile you can run a routine now, pick a skill's Response quality, and switch a skill's scheduled messages off and on.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.5
    • More of your agent's setup from your phone

      From Archie Mobile you can let in or block someone who messaged your agent, turn on calls to businesses, and paste your AI account's key. You can also change what Email Manager and Text Replies watch for, and say whose each mail account is.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.12
    • Short answers on your phone

      Text your agent from your phone and it answers in the first line and keeps the reply short, with no headings.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • When your chat app stops reaching your agent

      If messages on your chat app stop reaching your agent for more than half an hour, Archie tells you in Archie, and so on Archie Mobile, with what to do on the computer. It says so again once they get through.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.12

    Email

    • Email goes out when you send it or set a time

      Your agent drafts email replies and can't send one on its own. Each draft comes to your chat as a card with Send on it, and nothing leaves your account until you send it or set a time for it.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.1
    • Edit a draft in a pop-up

      Press Edit it on an email or text draft and a pop-up shows the message it answers. It has three ways to change the draft: type it your way, tell your agent what to change, or have it write three more.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Drafts waiting for you to press Send

      Every draft card says "Not sent yet." while it waits. Over the message box, a line such as "2 waiting to send" counts the drafts in this conversation, and pressing it opens the list.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.9
    • Write like me

      Turn on Write like me and give it some of your own writing: your sent mail, a document, or something you paste. When your agent drafts a reply, in chat, to mail that just arrived, or to a text, it writes it the way you write, and a text still reads like a text. You still read every draft before it goes.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.1
    • Text Replies on a Mac

      On a Mac, your agent reads texts as they arrive in Messages and offers a reply on a card when one needs an answer. Nothing sends until you press Send, and a reply goes out from your own number, as if you had typed it.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.4
    • Keep for every draft

      When you type your brokerage, phone number, or business name into a blank on an email draft, the card offers Keep for every draft.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.9
    • Stop watching your inbox

      When your agent starts reading your mail, it says in the chat which inboxes it reads and how often, with a Stop watching button.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.9
    • Mail from people you write to comes first

      Mail from someone you wrote to in the last two weeks is read at once; other mail can wait a few minutes, which lowers what your AI account is charged.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.9
    • Blanks in a draft

      Your agent leaves a blank in square brackets, like [her school], for a detail nobody gave, and an email or text with a blank in it will not send.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Check before sending

      On an email your agent drafts in chat, a price, a day, or a time that nobody gave it is listed under the draft for you to check.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.9
    • First text to a lead

      Ask your agent to text a lead, and it writes the text, says whether they agreed to texts, and puts a button under it so you can send it yourself.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.9
    • Known senders

      Before your agent reads an email, Archie checks whether you have the sender written down on your lists, on your agent, in what you have told your agent about your work, or as someone you wrote to lately.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.13
    • An email offers the change to your list

      When an email says something new about an entry on one of your lists, your agent puts the change on a card, and nothing changes until you press Update.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.2.1
    • A price nobody gave is left as a blank

      If a draft quotes a price not in what you typed, your lists, your files, or the email it answers, it is left in brackets and Send waits.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.13
    • Waiting on someone's answer

      When your agent is waiting on someone's answer, it watches for their next email or text, reads it when it comes, and tells you what came in and what it did, for 30 days unless it set another wait, 90 at most.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.3
    • The catch-up list after time away

      When Archie has not been running for an hour or more, the new mail and texts come as a list of up to six conversations, one list for each mailbox and one for texts, and picking one writes the reply for you to send.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.2.0
    • Read and left alone

      Email Manager and Text Replies each list the messages your agent read and decided not to tell you about, with who sent each, what it said and why it was left alone, for a day.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.2.1
    • When Archie can't read your email or your texts

      If Archie cannot read your email or your texts for half an hour, your agent tells you once in your chat, with what to do or that there is nothing to do, and again when it can. A mailbox that lost its place says which mail went unread.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.3
    • Email signatures per address, with a logo or a picture

      Each connected address signs with its own signature, which can include a logo or be a single picture at small, medium or large, previewed at the size that goes out, and on Archie for Teams a teammate can set the words of theirs by telling the agent.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.9
    • How much mail the agent tells you about and reads

      Two numbers on Email Manager and Text Replies cap how many messages an hour the agent tells you about and how many it reads at all, so attention and AI cost both have a ceiling. Past either number, new messages are not read, and are not read later.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.1.9
    • What the mail and text watches point out

      Email Manager and Text Replies point out someone new still waiting an hour, a reply you owe, and an email asking to change where a payment goes.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.13
    • A sent draft says it went

      Your agent's own words are never changed. When you press Send on an email it drafted, Archie says it went under the message that came with the draft: "Sent to Ace Septic at 8:01am."

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Asks before reading your mail

      Your agent reads your mail only after you say yes. With an email account and a skill that reads mail, it asks once in the chat, with Start reading my mail and Not now.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Mail filed away, and put back

      The agent can file mail into a folder you named or into Archive on Gmail, Outlook and the app-password providers, never deleting it, and each filing can be undone.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.3
    • Changing a waiting draft changes that draft

      While an email draft waits, asking for a new subject, asking your agent for a change, or replying to its card changes that draft instead of writing a second one. Nothing goes out until you press Send.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.2

    Calendar

    • Approve a calendar change

      When your agent wants to add, move or delete an event on a calendar you connected, it shows you the exact change and makes it only after you approve it in a later message. The exception is Yes, and stop asking, for some changes to your own calendar.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.1
    • Stop asking about your own calendar

      After you have said yes to three changes on your own calendar, the next card offers Yes, and stop asking. Press it and your agent adds and moves events on your own calendar that nobody else is on without asking first.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Your calendar is checked before a reply about a time

      When a text or an email asks about a time, your agent looks at your calendar before it writes the reply, so the draft won't say yes to a time you're already booked. When it offers to put something on your calendar, it tells you if that time is already taken.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.5
    • Invitations and a place on an event

      When your agent sets up a meeting, it can put the place on it and invite people once you say yes. The change it shows you first names everyone who will get an invitation, by name and email address.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Ask what's on, what's due, or what's free

      Ask about some days and Archie hands your agent what your lists, your calendar, and your reminders hold for those days before it answers.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Dates from your lists on the Calendar

      The Calendar tab shows the dates on your lists beside your calendar events, reminders, and routines, so a booking kept on a list shows on its day.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • A stop moved onto a busy day

      Move a stop to a day its truck or driver is on your calendar for something else, or a day that job already has a stop. Your agent tells you what is there and asks before moving it.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Where Bookings and your calendar differ

      On an event trailer agent, the morning list compares your Bookings list with your calendar for today and the next two weeks, and says where one has a booking the other does not. Ask what is on a day and your agent says the same.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11
    • A text or email that settles a new time becomes a calendar change you press

      When someone you're texting or emailing agrees on a new time, the agent puts a card in your chat offering to move the meeting on your calendar, or to add it when nothing is there. Nothing changes until you press it.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.19
    • The Calendar tab: your week in one place

      A week view, Sunday to Saturday, of the events on your connected calendars, your reminders, each routine's next run and the dates on your lists, in time order with a mark for each kind. It changes nothing on your calendar, and a reminder can be deleted there, with Undo. On Archie Mobile it is the next seven days, one under another.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.2.5

    Lists and to-dos

    • Your to-do list on the Dashboard

      Your to-do list is the first thing on your agent's Dashboard, where you can tick something off or add one without asking your agent.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.3
    • Stages on a list

      A list can show its steps, like Quoted, Booked, Out and Picked up, with each entry's step in color and a count at each step.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Lists in the sidebar and on the Dashboard

      Keep up to six lists in your agent's sidebar, under Jobs, and each one shows on the Dashboard with its count and where its entries stand.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Lists made from what you tell your agent

      When you first set up your agent and say what work you do, it drafts up to three lists that work runs on, with their steps.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Where you keep your work

      The last of your agent's first questions is where you keep your work today, with a button for each place, and its goodbye offers a way to bring in each of the first two.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Bring in a spreadsheet someone emailed

      Say "bring in the spreadsheet Dana emailed", and your agent finds the email, opens the file, and puts its rows on a card for you to add.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.9
    • Who owes you money

      Ask who owes you money, and your agent answers from entries on your lists marked billed and not paid, oldest first, with the days each has waited.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Fixing a save your agent claimed but never made

      If a reply says it put something on your lists and nothing was saved, Archie adds a line saying so, with Save it to save it now.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • A new list takes its first entries

      Ask for a new list and say what goes on it in the same message, and your agent makes the list and adds those entries in one reply.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Who to call

      Ask your agent who to call, and Archie works it out from your People and Deals lists: birthdays, closing anniversaries, quiet leads, and past clients.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Maybe already on a list

      When your agent adds someone, Archie looks on your lists for the same phone number, email, or name, and your agent says who it may be.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Hear when a booking puts something in two places

      When a booking puts a trailer or a unit in two places on the same day, Archie saves it as asked and says which booking it runs into.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Bring a spreadsheet into a list

      Import a spreadsheet into one of your lists. Archie matches the columns, leaves out rows already there, and names every cell it could not read.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Drop a spreadsheet in the chat

      Drop a spreadsheet into the chat and Archie puts up a card that names the list it fits and how many rows would come in.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Check new entries on one card before Add

      Hand your agent a photo, a page, or your calendar, and every entry it finds for one of your lists goes on one card you check before anything is added.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Bring a shared Google Sheet into a list

      Ask your agent to bring a Google Sheet you shared with it into one of your lists. The rows come in on a card you check first.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.8
    • How far along a list is

      Tell Archie about how many a list will hold, and it shows how many are entered so far, such as 25 of about 300 units entered.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Fold a row listed twice into one

      When a unit number or another value meant to be on a list once shows up twice, the list says so, and Review keeps the row you pick.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Ask about a unit by number

      Ask about unit 31 and your agent finds the row titled S-31, matching names like Trailer 4 or INV-1042 by their letters and numbers.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Keep a list matched to its spreadsheet

      Keep your own spreadsheet, and the list you brought in from it stays matched: Archie changes the list when you save the file, never changes your file, and asks before taking an entry off.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Asks before clearing what is filled in

      Your agent asks before it clears something already filled in on your lists, leaves a new entry's date blank when nothing you said gives one, and puts an entry you only asked about on a card to add with one press.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • A late pickup, asked about once a day

      Archie asks you about a late pickup for a rental at most once a day in the same chat, unless you bring that rental up.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Matching entries, added up in code

      When Archie looks up entries on one of your lists and two or more match, code adds up the number columns, like units and price. Your agent gets the totals, so it does not add them itself.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Units out, counted place by place

      When Archie looks up the units you have out, code counts them place by place against the rentals running there today. Your agent hears where your two lists agree, where they differ, and by how many.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Save a list as a spreadsheet

      Save as a spreadsheet on a list writes the whole list to a CSV file you can open in Excel, Numbers or Google Sheets.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.2.0
    • A list column can point at another list

      A column can point at another list, so an entry picks a row from it (a task names its project). From 0.3.9 your agent finds the entries by that row's name, so what is left on a project has an answer.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.2.4
    • Totals from your lists are added up in code

      Ask for a total from one of your lists and Archie adds the numbers itself rather than leaving the sum to the AI.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.7
    • Todoist and Google Tasks: check off or edit at once, with Undo

      Checking off or editing a to-do in Todoist or Google Tasks happens right away, with an Undo that puts it back (a repeating Todoist task goes back on its repeat, counted from today). Adding one has no Undo, and deleting one still waits for your yes.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.7
    • Taking something off a list, and putting it back

      Ask your agent to take an entry off a list and it goes at once, with Undo for 30 days. A question, more than 10 at once, or emptying a list of two or more entries still waits for your yes. A teammate's ask waits for their own yes, and a routine's removal waits on a card for you to press.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.19
    • Statements read like the last one

      Ask your agent to change one of its add-on's settings, or a line in how it talks or who it serves, and it does, says what changed, and puts it back if you say undo.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.16
    • Choose what your agent can do

      Switches decide what your agent offers, such as setting reminders or reading the web; turn one off and each message costs a little less.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.0
    • What your agent will never do

      Your agent is awake only when you write, a routine's time comes, or it checks a mailbox you connected. It cannot run a command or text anyone.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.3
    • The crisis floor

      If you tell your agent you are thinking about hurting yourself, or someone is putting you in danger, it steps out of character and names where to get help.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.3
    • Who stopped an agent, and when

      A stopped agent says who stopped it and when, such as "You stopped Ember yesterday at 11:34 PM", in Archie and in Archie Mobile.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Payment instructions are never passed on

      If an email, document, or message gives new or changed payment or wiring instructions, your agent is told never to pass them on, even if you ask.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • A change you did not ask for is offered, not made

      Ask your agent to change one thing on a list and it changes that. If it also wants to move something you didn't mention, like a client to Past client, it asks first, with buttons like Change it to Past client and Keep Active. A payment that could belong to either of two entries waits for you to say which.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.13
    • Undo that, answered with what was changed

      Type undo that, and Archie says exactly what your agent changed the last time you asked it for something, with an Undo button for each change. Nothing is put back until you press one.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.13
    • GoHighLevel changes made at once, with Undo

      On Archie for Teams, every GoHighLevel change waits for a yes until the agent's owner turns on one of two kinds: moving a deal to another stage, or filling in a contact's custom fields. With one on, a change somebody asks for by name is made right away, and the line under the reply says what changed and what it was before, with Undo.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.16

    Privacy and security

    • Where your conversations go

      On your own AI account, what you write goes straight from your computer to that AI company, and Otian is not in the middle and keeps no copy.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.1
    • No analytics, and crash reports you can turn off

      Archie has no analytics service, and its version check-in and its crash and error reports carry your account ID but never anything you wrote, received, or asked for.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.3
    • The update check

      Archie checks for updates with a plain request that carries no version number, nothing identifying your computer, and no account.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.1.1
    • Where your keys are kept

      The keys you save for AI companies and services are kept in your computer's built-in password store, where we have no way to read them.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.1
    • The access record

      Archie writes down each time a saved key is used and each change to who or what can reach your agents, and shows if any line was changed.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.1.1
    • No list of the add-ons you install

      Adding an add-on raises its public popularity count by one, and we keep only the running total, never a list of which add-ons are yours.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.1.1
    • What Archie Mobile asks for on your phone

      Archie Mobile uses the camera, your photos, your files and the microphone only when you press to scan, pick, take or record something.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.1
    • Reset Archie

      Reset Archie erases your agents and your saved keys from your computer, disconnects every phone, and empties the phone mailbox.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.1.3
    • How long the phone mailbox keeps things

      Messages between Archie Mobile and your computer wait in a mailbox on Otian's server. The phone deletes each once read, and your computer clears leftovers a day later.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.2.5
    • What listens on your computer

      Nothing on the network can reach Archie. Only three things listen, on your computer and only while in use: a sign-in, the Google Drive picker, and the Computer control browser.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.1
    • An address your agent came up with waits for your yes

      Your agent opens a web page on its own only when the address came from you, from a page it already opened, or from a site you named in your message. An address it came up with itself, it shows you first and waits for your yes.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.5
    • How did you hear about Archie

      On the Account page, Archie asks how you heard about it, and sends nothing unless you press an answer, which is then kept on your account.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.10
    • Where your information goes guide

      A guide that says what stays on your computer, what goes to your AI company and to Otian AI, what our servers hold, and how to turn each off.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Ask where your information goes

      Ask your agent where your information goes, who can see it, or whether anyone trains on it, and it answers in the guide's own words without asking an AI company.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • What connecting email means

      Before you connect your email, Archie says what your agent reads and when, where that goes, what it never does, and how to switch it off.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.9
    • The safety checklist

      Four things worth doing once outside Archie (two-step verification on your chat app and on your connected accounts, a spending limit with your AI company, and locking this computer), each saying what goes wrong if left undone, with a link to the company's own page for your chat app and your AI company where Archie knows it.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.1.3
    • A text with a sign-in code or a PIN is kept from the AI

      A text with a sign-in code, or a PIN beside its number, is dropped on your Mac as it arrives, before the AI reads it, and is never answered. It is kept out of what the AI reads later too: the earlier messages under a newer text, and the texts you send.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.1.4
    • What the technical log holds, and mail that came while Archie was off

      The technical log holds who each email was from, its subject line, and a short summary of each email or text your agent left alone, never the full text of one. After Archie has been off, your agent reads what came in while it was off, if that was under about a week.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.6
    • Your agent answers you and nobody else

      In Archie, each agent answers only the one person who claimed it. Anyone else who writes to it is told the agent is private, gets no answer from your agent, and is listed on the agent's Setup tab so you can block them.

      • On your computer
      • Not in Archie for Teams
      • Since 0.1.4

    Plans

    • The plan with the AI included

      For $59 a month or $599 a year, Archie comes with $25 of Claude usage each month, so you need no AI account of your own.

      • On your computer
      • Not in Archie for Teams
      • Since 0.2.3
    • A 14-day trial on your own AI account

      When a computer has used its free credits, you can still try Archie for 14 days by connecting an AI account of your own.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.1.3
    • What Archie costs, on screen

      During a free trial, a strip at the bottom of the window says what Archie costs afterward, and the Account page's Your plan row says the same.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Ask what Archie costs

      Ask your agent what Archie costs or the cheapest way to keep going, and Archie answers from its own price list without asking the AI.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.9
    • Add your AI account after buying a plan

      Buy a plan without the AI in it, and Archie asks for your AI account next, so your first agent starts as soon as it is made.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Free on your own AI account, 20 jobs a day

      Paste a key from an AI company and Archie opens for free, with every skill and routine, up to 20 jobs a day. A plan takes the limit off.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Not in Archie for Teams
      • Since 0.3.0
    • Your plan follows your Otian account

      A plan lives on your Otian account, so signing in on another computer gets the same plan.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.1.3
    • What happens when a plan ends

      A plan you stop runs to the end of the period you paid for. Nothing on your computer is deleted, and what opens next depends on your edition and key.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.0
    • When the free trial ends

      Three days before your free trial ends, and again the day before, your agent tells you the day and the time in your chat app. In Archie, what needs no AI keeps running after it ends.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.13
    • The spend note in chat

      A week after your agent's first call on your own AI account, it says in chat what it has cost and what that comes to a month, then again 30 days after that first call and every 30 days after. Archie works the figure out with no AI, and says nothing when it cannot price something.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.2.4
    • Tell us a job went wrong

      Open a job on the Jobs tab and press Tell us it went wrong. Archie shows you the job's record, then opens it in your own email app addressed to us, and Jett or Jack reads it.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.19

    Archie for Teams

    • Archie and Archie for Teams on one computer

      Archie for Teams installs beside Archie as its own app, with its own data and its own keys, so one computer can run both.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.2.5
    • Move your agents into Archie for Teams

      When you hire, save a backup in Archie and open it in Archie for Teams, and your agents arrive with their knowledge, lists, routines and memory.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Team Starter pack

      A new Archie for Teams agent starts with Team Starter: a shared to-do list, a record of who took which job, web lookups, and a personality naming who it answers.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Write down who each teammate is

      When you add someone, write down their name and what they do, and an email or phone number if you like. Your agent then knows who is on the team, so asked to write to Dana it already has her address.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.8
    • A teammate on Archie Mobile, with no chat app

      Add someone to your agent without asking them to set up Telegram or Slack. Archie makes a link for that one person, and you send it however you like. They get Archie Mobile, paste the link, and talk to your agent from their own phone, with no account to make.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.9
    • Choose what teammates can do

      On a shared agent you choose what the people you let in can do: ask it things, also add to and change its lists, or everything you can. In the middle setting a teammate can log a delivery or add a task to the agent's lists, and still cannot send your mail, change your calendar, or use the apps you connected.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.7
    • Owner, admins and teammates

      Everybody on an agent has a role. The owner is who the agent works for, and its routines report to them. An admin can change the agent and decide who is on it, the same as the owner, and whoever set it up can make the right person the owner.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.10
    • Add and edit people from your phone

      In Archie Mobile, under More, then Teammates, you can add someone, edit their name and contact details, take them off, or stop a waiting invite. You copy or share the invite message from your phone.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.9
    • Teammates set and cancel reminders for themselves

      A teammate can ask your agent to remind them of something, and it reminds them in the chat they asked in, never on your to-do list. They can cancel their own reminders and nobody else's.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Your team this week

      Your agent's Dashboard lists your team: what each person does, how many messages they sent the agent this week and how many jobs those started, and when they last wrote. Press a name to read what they said.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.8
    • See what a teammate can see

      Press What Dana can see beside anyone you added. Archie lists the mailboxes, calendars and apps your agent can use for them, what it keeps that they can ask about, and what they can change.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.8
    • A teammate asking about the work gets their own entries

      When a teammate asks your agent about a list that says whose each entry is, they hear about their own entries and the ones with nobody named, and an entry they add is theirs. You still see every entry.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Websites for a teammate

      On Archie for Teams, a teammate on Everything you can can have your agent use websites, in a separate browser window that is not signed in to anything.

      • On your computer
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.12
    • What a teammate saved, told to you

      When someone on your team tells your agent something that adds to or changes one of your lists, you get a message saying what they saved. Under their reply, they see that you are told.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.11
    • The owner can read what a shared agent said to everybody else

      On an agent other people can message, the owner can read each person's conversation with it, with no box to type into, and someone let in on a chat app or on Archie Mobile is told before their first answer that the owner can read what they write.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.1.9
    • The Company page on Archie for Teams

      Archie for Teams shows every agent in the company on one page, what each is for, and which agent keeps, adds to or only reads each list, and a skill or routine can be moved from one agent to another there.

      • On your computer
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.1.5
    • What the Marketplace holds on Archie for Teams

      The Marketplace in Archie for Teams holds the add-ons built for a team, plus everything a business and a person can both use. The home-life ones, like Meal Planner and Home Workout Coach, are in Archie instead.

      • On your computer
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.0
    • A mail account marked as one person's

      On Archie for Teams, a connected account starts out shared, so your agent can answer anyone you let in from it, its mail included. Mark it as one person's with Whose is this?, and only that person is answered from it.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.1.5
    • Your company's name and logo stay on this computer

      On Archie for Teams, put your company's name and a logo on the Company page. Archie shows them there and in its sidebar, and sends them nowhere, your AI company included.

      • On your computer
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.0

    Archie on your computer

    • Right-click an agent

      Right-click an agent in Archie to open it, start or stop it, rename it, change how it looks, or delete it.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Keeps running with the window closed

      Close Archie's window and your agent keeps working. Archie stays running in the Dock on a Mac, or by the clock on Windows, until you quit it.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.9
    • Opens at login

      Archie opens by itself, with no window, when you sign in to your computer, so your agent is answering again after a restart.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.9
    • Open Archie with a few keys

      By default, press Control, Shift and Space on a Mac, or Ctrl, Alt and Space on Windows, and Archie comes forward on your last chat, ready to type.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Archie in the Mac menu bar

      On a Mac, Archie has an icon in the menu bar at the top of the screen that opens it or quits it.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Bring an agent over from OpenClaw

      Archie reads your OpenClaw agent's folder on this computer and shows you what it would make before it makes anything. Its personality, what it knows about you, its notes, its skills and its scheduled jobs become the new agent's.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.1
    • The Jobs tab: your agent's jobs, step by step, with Undo

      Your agent's jobs are on a board of four columns (Scheduled, Working, Needs you, Done), each titled in your words or with the routine's name, with each change it made and an Undo on each change that can be taken back.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.3
    • Start a new agent from one you already have

      Making a second agent can start from an existing one, with its skills, routines, way of talking and what it knows about you, so it is the first agent pointed at a different job. Connected accounts carry over; who may message it and its conversations do not.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.1.3
    • The agent's face: Ember in your colors, or your own photo

      Each agent wears Ember, the app's drawn character, in a color, hat, eyes and extra you pick, or a photo you bring, made on this computer with no image model, and Discord and Matrix bots take the same picture.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.3
    • The Dashboard: what needs you today

      The agent opens on one screen of what needs you: a draft to send, a change to approve, or a problem to fix, each with a button that answers it or takes you to where it is answered; your to-do list, with your reminders on it; your lists; and what the agent is doing this minute.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.2.5
    • A guide for moving your agent to a computer that stays home

      A guide in Archie walks through moving the agent to a computer that stays home and on, so it keeps working when the laptop is closed.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.12
    • Theme, and the Mac look

      Pick Light, Dark or Automatic from pictures. On a Mac, Archie uses the system font and a see-through sidebar, of Liquid Glass on macOS 26 and later, that follows the Mac's own Liquid Glass setting in System Settings.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.1
    • A screen reader hears what your agent is doing, then its answer

      With VoiceOver or another screen reader on, Archie says when your agent starts working and the first thing it is doing, then reads the answer as soon as it is done.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.13
    • When Archie is slow to open

      If Archie takes longer than usual to open, it says so. After a minute it offers Try again and Get help, and Get help starts an email to us with what it saw.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Opening Archie again brings the open copy forward on Windows

      On Windows, opening Archie while it is already running brings the open window forward instead of starting a second copy.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.6
    • The Dashboard card's sky follows the time of day

      The status card at the top of the Dashboard has a sky that changes with the clock on this device, with no weather and no location asked.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.12
